referenceFunction.generalComment: This dataset represents the activity of waste disposal of excavation material, clean in a excavation landfill. Recommended use of this dataset: For unrecycled, clean excavation material being landfilled. Not suitable for polluted excavation material.Inventoried waste consists of fraction: 100% excavation material, clean; . referenceFunction.includedProcesses: Waste-specific short-term emissions via landfill leachate. Waste-specific long-term emissions from landfill. Land transformation and occupation. Waste placement and compaction. Landfill construction materials, sewer pipe for leachate, and access road.
referenceFunction.localName: Disposal, excavation material, clean, 20% water, to excavation landfill
referenceFunction.name: Disposal, excavation material, clean, 20% water, to excavation landfill

technology.text: This is an inventory for a excavation landfill (cleanfill, VVEA type A). Ultimate average landfill height is 11 meters. Operation phase duration is 15 years.

representativeness.samplingProcedure: Landfill model based on average composition of landfilled excavation material and observed average leachate concentrations from various literature sources. Extrapolated to 60'000 years heeding chemical characteristics and hydrology. Based on waste composition and climate data the end of carbonate phase of this landfill is estimated to be reached 10849 years after waste deposition.
representativeness.uncertaintyAdjustments: uncertainty of waste input composition data derived from generic formula GSD(c) = N*ln(c)+1. *Mean* long-term emissions are the emissions until 60'000 years after waste placement. *Maximal* (upper bound) long-term emissions are the complete emissions of all landfilled material, depicting possible mechanical landfill failures and/or natural erosion not heeded in the mean value. Minimal long-term emissions are derived implicitly from the mean and maximal values assuming a lognormal distribution.
